pr_body:
Fixes #72700.

We released contention views in 21.2, later discovering we mis-scoped
the query backing `crdb_internal.cluster_contended_indexes`.

This change corrects the scoping and also sorts the results usefully.

Release note (bug fix): the query backing
crdb_internal.cluster_contended_indexes improperly assumed that index
ids were unique across the database. This change adds the proper scoping
by table descriptor id, truing up the contents of that view.

issue_context.title: 21.2 Contention view returns incorrect results
issue_context.body:
We released contention views (contended indexes) in 21.2: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/61507. An issue has been reported where this view would be returning wrong results. 

Doc issue outlining the issue: https://github.com/cockroachdb/docs/issues/12269

We need to correlate the contention_event's table id with table_index's descriptor id. Feedback also mentioned we should have the results DESC order.

Two options:

SELECT DISTINCT t.database_name, t.schema_name, t.name, ti.index_name, ce.num_contention_events
FROM crdb_internal.cluster_contention_events ce
INNER JOIN crdb_internal.table_indexes ti
  ON ce.index_id = ti.index_id
AND ce.table_id = ti.descriptor_id
INNER JOIN crdb_internal.tables t
  ON ce.table_id = t.table_id 
ORDER BY ce.num_contention_events DESC;

OR

SELECT DISTINCT database_name, schema_name, name, index_name, num_contention_events
FROM crdb_internal.cluster_contention_events, crdb_internal.tables, crdb_internal.table_indexes
WHERE (crdb_internal.cluster_contention_events.index_id = crdb_internal.table_indexes.index_id AND crdb_internal.cluster_contention_events.table_id = crdb_internal.table_indexes.descriptor_id)
AND (crdb_internal.cluster_contention_events.table_id = crdb_internal.tables.table_id)
ORDER BY num_contention_events DESC;
